host.note: Reconstructed session: the replies were written by an agent playing this session; every embed was computed by the host from the graphs named.

turns.request: Open the Snowdon model. What does it hold?
turns.reply: Only the architectural discipline is registered on this host (Snowdon Towers Sample Architectural.bos, 30,760 elements); the seven-discipline federation TKT-30 describes isn't wired in here, so this session works from that one file. 96 Revit categories. The largest are Pipes (3,051), Analytical Surfaces (3,041), and Supports (2,779) — mechanical and analytical content dominates the count, not the architecture. Doors: 142. Rooms: 54. Spaces: 236.

turns.request: How many doors and how many spaces?
turns.reply: 142 doors. Rooms and Spaces are separate Revit categories here — 54 Rooms and 236 Spaces, 290 together, both meaning occupiable area rather than a building element.

turns.request: Rooms per storey, as a chart.
turns.reply: 33 storeys carry at least one room, out of 84 levels total (the rest are reference planes, pits, and roof datums with no rooms). L1 - Block 43 has the most, 26; L4 follows at 20 and 15 on its two passes (the model splits some levels into more than one named block at the same elevation, so a level name can appear twice in the chart).

turns.request: Doors narrower than 850 mm on L1 - Block 43, the tallest bar on that chart.
turns.reply: Clicking that bar selects L1 - Block 43, its 26 rooms and 10 doors. No door on this storey carries a leaf clear-width parameter (this model has no OverallWidth-equivalent), so DC-W1 as written can't run here. The closest available measure is Rough Width, the framed opening rather than the leaf: 4 of the 10 doors carry it (1,016 mm, 1,016 mm, 978 mm, 978 mm — all at or above 850 mm), and the other 6, all curtain-wall storefront doors plus one 60" x 84" pair, carry no width parameter at all and come back InfoNotAvailable rather than a guessed Pass or Fail. Nothing on this storey measures narrower than 850 mm by the one width this model has.
